body.statement: For the finite inputs \(K,L,y,p^{1:L},N,\alpha\), the \(4K\) Clopper--Pearson intervals, and the generated component arrays \(A_\gamma,B_\gamma,b_\gamma,C_\gamma\), the finite common-rank inversion algorithm terminates and returns: an exact finite-union extended formulation of \(C_n\); an exact common-parameter finite-union representation of every member of \(\mathcal H_n\); and the exact radii \(r_n^{\mathrm{out}}\) and \(r_n^{\mathrm{set}}\). Its outputs equal the objects in the outer-inversion and inversion-radii definitions, including the deterministic fallback when \(R_n\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}=\varnothing\). In the unit-cost ordered-field model it uses at most \[(2m_{\mathrm{alg}}|\Gamma_K|)^{2^{O(v_{\mathrm{alg}})}}\] arithmetic and order operations, where \(|\Gamma_K|\le(2L+1)^2\binom{2K-2}{K-1}\); hence the procedure is finite for every fixed input.
body.justification: The theorem turns the nonconvex path representation into a terminating exact procedure for both reported confidence objects and their metric informativeness.
body.gap: Finite categorical instrumental-variable programs handle one convex compatibility region; they do not compute Hausdorff radii for a common-parameter collection of law-dependent nonconvex path unions.
body.consumer: Oregon Medicaid analysts can compute exact outer regions and diagnose their Hausdorff width before reporting extrapolations at support boundaries.
